findings.title: Materials' 52-point lens gap signals distress
findings.body: Materials trades at 16.96x forward but 35.71x trailing, a 52-point percentile gap — the widest in the table. The market is pricing an 111 percent earnings rebound, which is a bet on a sharp cyclical recovery rather than a reflection of current profitability.

findings.title: Health Care hits all-time forward richness
findings.body: Health Care's forward multiple sits at the 100th percentile of its five-year range, yet its trailing multiple is only at the 82nd. The 45 percent compression between lenses implies analysts expect 80 percent earnings growth, an aggressive underwriting that leaves no room for disappointment.

findings.title: Utilities' trailing percentile collapses to 2
findings.body: Utilities' forward P/E of 17.51 is at the 28th percentile, but its trailing multiple of 18.24 sits at the 2nd percentile — a 26-point gap. That near-floor trailing reading suggests reported earnings have been unusually strong, making the forward multiple look less cheap than its own history implies.
